extracted.intended_audience: public-sector decision makers and practitioners (local/state/federal government leaders, digital services, IT, communications, and service design teams)
extracted.subtask_description: Selecting, designing, or evaluating digital government platforms and services to modernize service delivery, improve engagement, and increase operational efficiency across jurisdictions. Focuses on outcomes, channels, accessibility, automation, and data-driven insights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational efficiency / reduced staff time
rubrics_metrics.description: Reduce staff time through efficiency and automation (claims of 'Do more with what you have' and '80% Reduced staff time through efficiency').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include automating public records requests, meetings and agenda management, short-term rental compliance, and other complex, time‑intensive tasks; Granicus cites increases in operational efficiency of 25–80% and specific case studies (e.g., Parachute, CO) as evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improve service delivery and user satisfaction
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve service delivery to provide a better experience for constituents and increase user satisfaction (noted '70% Increase in user satisfaction').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measured through user satisfaction metrics and case studies (e.g., Gainesville, FL). Improvements come from digitizing services, streamlining workflows, and designing for user needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reach and engagement (audience scale)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grow reach and engage community members at scale ('100X Community members reached and engaged', '1M+ Subscribers engaging on critical issues').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use customer experience services, opt-in subscriber networks, and multi-channel campaigns to move audiences from awareness to action; examples include large subscription growth for campaigns and program adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase in service adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Drive adoption of government services ('275% Increase in service adoption').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adoption increases via targeted outreach, better UX, and integrated digital services—illustrated through success stories where Engagement Cloud and GXG increased adoption and subscriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and inclusive design
rubrics_metrics.description: Build inclusive digital services that serve the whole community 'where they are, on their terms' including language and accessibility tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Features called out include automated language and accessibility tools; guidance references resources like 'Navigating accessibility: Building inclusive digital services for the future.' Accessibility is positioned as necessary for wide community reach and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-channel delivery and device optimization
rubrics_metrics.description: Deliver services and communications across channels and devices (meetings online and on-demand; email and SMS messaging; information hubs optimized for desktop and mobile).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serve constituents through the channels they prefer—examples include on-demand meetings, SMS/email outreach, and mobile‑optimized information hubs to increase engagement and satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: 24/7 self-service via AI-powered agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide continuous self-service access to jurisdictionally relevant information via AI agents ('Give your residents...24/7 access' with the Government Experience Agent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes reducing friction for residents and call centers; guidance includes piloting AI agents (see 'Proven playbook: How governments can run a high‑impact AI agent pilot') and focusing on jurisdictional accuracy and purpose-built design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy and jurisdictional relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure information provided is accurate and jurisdictionally relevant (explicitly called out for the AI agent).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI agents and digital channels should deliver the 'most accurate, jurisdictionally relevant information' to avoid resident frustration and reduce contact center loads.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience growth and targeted outreach
rubrics_metrics.description: Grow and convert audiences using human-centered strategies and targeted outreach ('combines human-centered strategies with our 330 million-strong opt-in subscriber network to grow your audience').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use targeted outreach strategies, two-way feedback channels, and data to move people from awareness to action; case studies (Veterans Affairs, Manchester, CT) illustrate tactics and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data-driven insights, benchmarking, and analytics
rubrics_metrics.description: Use data and benchmarking to understand performance and identify opportunities (e.g., '2026 State of Digital Government Report', 'Data-driven insights for modern government').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produce reports and metrics, run analytics (GXI Enterprise/GXI Foundations), and use trends/benchmarks to prioritize improvements and measure ROI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce in-person visits and cost savings
rubrics_metrics.description: Digitize services to reduce walk-ins and lower costs ('See 80% fewer walk-ins, reduce costs, generate revenue').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital permitting, licensing, 311/service requests, and online forms reduce demand on front offices and can recover revenue while improving access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamline compliance and records management
rubrics_metrics.description: Improve compliance and transform records/short-term rental (STR) management and public records workflows ('Transform records and STR management', 'Public records & STR compliance').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Automate records requests and compliance workflows to increase efficiency and reduce risk; includes special product references like GovQA and Host Compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency to increase participation
rubrics_metrics.description: Increase transparency (e.g., in election processes) to drive civic participation and trust ('increased transparency in the vote‑by‑mail process, which led to higher turnout').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use communications platforms and engagement tools to surface transparent information; case study (King County Elections) shows transparency as an engagement lever.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized communications and responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Centralize constituent communications to enable swift response across channels ('Centralizing constituent communications for swift response across all channels').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralization supports consistent messaging, faster citizen response, and better coordination across agencies and channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usability and seamless integration
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide usable experiences with fewer clicks and seamless interoperability ('Fewer clicks, more compliant' and 'everything will work seamlessly together').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on information architecture, streamlined user journeys, and integrated product suites (meetings, websites, records) to reduce friction and increase compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pilot governance and playbook for AI initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Run well‑structured AI agent pilots using a proven playbook ('Proven playbook: How governments can run a high‑impact AI agent pilot').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes staged pilots, measurement, and operational considerations for AI deployment; use playbooks and case studies to guide governance, evaluation, and scaling.
